newsitem.title: USA: Ivax in deal to sell McGaw unit for $400 mln.
newsitem.headline: Ivax in deal to sell McGaw unit for $400 mln.

text.p: Ivax Corp said Friday it has signed a definitive agreement to sell its McGaw Inc unit to B. Braun of America Inc, a unit of B. Braun Melsungen AG, a privately owned medical products manufacturer in Germany.
Ivax, a holding company based in Miami, Fla., said B. Braun will pay approximately $320 million in cash at closing, subject to post-closing adjustments.

Over a period of unspecified years, B. Braun will make additional payments of up to $80 million, contingent on the combined operating results of McGaw and B. Braun's main U.S. operating unit B. Braun Medical Inc, it said.

Ivax said it will also receive royalties and other payments based on McGaw's and B. Braun's commercialization of the Duplex drug delivery system. Duplex, which is under development, is an intravenous drug delivery system designed for intravenous drugs that have limited stability after mixing.

McGaw, which is based in Irvine, Calif., makes intravenous solutions and ralated products. B. Braun of America, based in Bethlehem, Pa., makes disposable medical products for hospitals and other markets.
